items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: the first time we went in there we had Sid Catlett, John Simmons, Charlie Christian, Cootie Williams, five or six black guys

ctx.x: Well, I think music owes a lot to him. He's been very good to us through the ways in which -- black musicians. He was the first bandleader to make that giant step of putting them in his band, putting a black person in his band, which was Teddy Wilson, I believe. And I know, I've known him all my life since we were little kids. And I've worked for him and we've disagreed a million or more times. But just recently I had somebody ask me to name 10 people that I would put in a Hall of Fame and of course, I named…

Yes. And of course, he stuck his neck out. You know, Benny is a very mercenary man, he's very interested in money. But he cut off almost half the country for that man. He didn't want to travel in the South with the band so he cut off a large part of his income. And I've heard him stand up, even in the New Yorker, the first time we went in there we had Sid Catlett, John Simmons, Charlie Christian, Cootie Williams, five or six black guys, I don't remember all. You know, you're working in a band, you forget who's…
who's white. You know, you've got to start visualizing which is which. You see somebody enough, they don't have a color anymore.
